b: I’m re-reading “Castles of Steel” by Robert Massie. If his writing is to be believed, Churchill basically had the right idea. Force the narrows quickly before the Turks can reinforce them. Land sufficient troops to hold. Instead, de Robeck and Hamilton delay, and it becomes Kitchener’s show to lead into disaster.

So why does Churchill get the blame? Is this a case where one history (this book) is not in line with accepted scholarship? I’m not asking what would have happened if the straits had been forced, but if the plan that failed wasn’t Churchill’s then why does he still get blamed for it? In period, I get it, but if historians have access to Turkish and German documents later, why still blame the First Lord?
